lessons.title: Straight Lines
lessons.summary: Pull clean, confident lines in one move.

steps.title: Pull, don't push
steps.text: Wobbly lines happen when we draw slowly using only our fingers. Instead, move your whole arm from the shoulder and pull the line in one quick, smooth move. Watch: the line starts gently, speeds up, and lands right on the end dot.

steps.title: Ghost it first
steps.text: Before you touch the screen, hover your pencil over the path and practice the move two or three times. This is called ghosting. Once your arm knows the way, put the pencil down and draw it in one go.

steps.title: Across
steps.text: Start on the left dot and pull straight across to the right dot.
steps.hint: Ghost the move first, then draw it in one quick pull without stopping.

steps.title: Down
steps.text: Now from the top dot straight down to the bottom dot.
steps.hint: Keep your wrist still and move your whole arm down.

steps.title: Slant
steps.text: A slanted line from the bottom left dot up to the top right dot.
steps.hint: Turn the iPad if a different angle feels easier. Artists do it all the time!

quiz.question: What helps you draw a straighter line?
choices: Drawing very slowly with your fingertips
One quick, steady pull with your whole arm
quiz.explain: A quick pull from the shoulder keeps the line steady from start to end.

lessons.title: Curves & Circles
lessons.summary: Smooth curves and circles that close up.

steps.title: One smooth turn
steps.text: A circle is one line that keeps curving by the same amount all the way round. Start at the top, keep your speed steady, and finish exactly where you began.

steps.title: C-curve
steps.text: Trace the C. Keep the speed steady so the curve stays smooth.
steps.hint: Move your whole arm and don't stop halfway round.

steps.title: Circle
steps.text: Start at the dot on top, go all the way round, and end where you started.
steps.hint: Ghost the circle in the air a couple of times first, then draw.

steps.title: Oval
steps.text: An oval is a stretched circle. Same trick: one smooth loop.
steps.hint: Go a little faster along the long sides.

quiz.question: Your circle has a gap where the ends don't meet. What's the best fix?
choices: Leave the gap, nobody will notice
Redraw it in one smooth loop and end where you started
Draw lots of short lines to fill the gap
quiz.explain: One smooth loop that ends where it began gives a clean, closed circle.

lessons.title: Waves & S-Curves
lessons.summary: Lines with rhythm, like water and tails.

steps.title: Lines with rhythm
steps.text: Lots of things move in waves: water, flags, hair, a cat's tail. An S-curve bends one way, then the other. Keep your hand moving at a steady speed and let the line flow.

steps.title: S-curve
steps.text: Trace the S from top to bottom in one move.
steps.hint: Let your wrist swing gently left, then right, as your arm moves down.

steps.title: Waves
steps.text: Ride the waves from left to right.
steps.hint: Keep the tops and the dips the same height.

steps.title: Spiral
steps.text: Start in the middle and spiral outward.
steps.hint: Turn the page with your other hand if it helps, and keep the gaps even.

quiz.question: Which of these moves like a wave?
quiz.explain: Wind sends ripples along a flag, just like an S-curve repeating.

steps.title: Corners and sides
steps.text: Shapes with corners, like squares and triangles, are just straight lines that meet. Draw each side as its own quick line, and make sure the corners touch so the shape is closed with no gaps.

steps.title: Square
steps.text: Trace the square. You can draw it as four lines or one.
steps.hint: Stop exactly on each corner before you start the next side.

steps.title: Triangle
steps.text: Three sides, three corners. Close it up!
steps.hint: Start at the top point and go round.

steps.title: House
steps.text: Shapes can join up to make things. Trace the house, its roof and its door.
steps.hint: Draw the big square first, then the roof on top, then the door.

quiz.question: Why do closed shapes matter when you color with the paint bucket?
choices: The color leaks out through any gap
quiz.explain: The paint bucket fills inside the lines. If there's a gap, the color spills out across the page.

lessons.title: Thick & Thin Lines
lessons.summary: Line weight makes drawings feel deep.

steps.title: Line weight
steps.text: Line weight means how thick a line is. Thick lines feel close, heavy or in shadow. Thin lines feel far away or light. With Apple Pencil, press harder for a thicker line.

steps.title: Taper your lines
steps.text: A line that starts thin, gets thicker in the middle and ends thin looks alive. Start gently, press in the middle, then lift off at the end. Here's the shape a tapered line makes.

steps.title: Leaf
steps.text: Trace the leaf: two curves that meet at the tips, then the line down the middle.
steps.hint: Try pressing lightly at the tips and harder in the middle.

steps.title: Feel the pressure
steps.text: Try line weight in your own drawing.

tasks: Open a project and pick the Ink Brush.
Draw a line pressing very lightly.
Now draw one line that starts light, presses in the middle and ends light.

quiz.question: You want a tree to look far away. What lines should you use?
quiz.explain: Thin, light lines make things feel further away.

lessons.title: Build With Shapes
lessons.summary: Turn circles, ovals and triangles into a cat.

steps.title: Everything is shapes
steps.text: Artists don't draw a cat all at once. They start with simple shapes: a circle for the head, an oval for the body, triangles for the ears. Then they add details on top. Watch the cat get built.

steps.title: The head
steps.text: Start with the head: a circle and two triangle ears.
steps.hint: Draw the circle first, then the ears.

steps.title: The body
steps.text: Now the oval body and a curvy tail.
steps.hint: Keep the oval smooth, then flick the tail up.

steps.title: The whole cat
steps.text: Put it all together: head, ears, body, tail and legs.
steps.hint: Big shapes first, small shapes last.

quiz.question: What should you draw first?
choices: Big simple shapes like circles and ovals
The fur, one hair at a time
quiz.explain: Big shapes first set the size and pose. Details go on top at the end.
